title: Achieving Better Local Regret Bound for Online Non-Convex Bilevel Optimization
claim: Our proposed method attains lower regret and loss and competitive accuracy than baselines across online streaming iterations.
layout: 3 line plots in a row, shared iteration axis, legend in each
description: Three side-by-side line charts share the same x-axis, iteration from 0 to 3000, and the same five-method legend: AOBO, OBBO, SOBOW, FSOBO and SOGD. AOBO is drawn as a solid blue line. The left panel plots bilevel local regret on a log scale. AOBO grows slowest and ends lowest, and OBBO ends highest at about 100. The middle panel plots corrupted loss. It drops sharply and spikes at iterations 1000 and 2000, which look like distribution shifts. AOBO recovers fastest and sits lowest. The right panel plots test accuracy, which dips at the same shift points. All methods end near 0.87 to 0.88, and AOBO rises fastest at the start. The grid is light and the lines carry different markers and dash styles.
caption: Performance of different algorithms on the online hyper-cleaning.
abstract: Online bilevel optimization (OBO) has emerged as a powerful framework for many machine learning problems. Prior works have developed several algorithms that minimize the standard bilevel local regret or the window-averaged bilevel local regret of the OBO problem, but the optimality of existing regret bounds remains unclear. In this work, we establish optimal regret bounds for both settings. For standard bilevel local regret, we propose an algorithm with adaptive iteration strategy that achieves the optimal regret $Î©(1+V_T)$ with at most $O(T\log T)$ total inner-level gradient evaluations. We further develop a fully single-loop algorithm whose regret bound includes an additional gradient-variation terms. For the window-averaged bilevel local regret, we design an algorithm that captures linear environmental variation through a novel window-based analysis and achieves the optimal regret $Î©(T/W^2)$. The algorithm also supports an efficient single-loop structure, achieving an $O(T/W)$ regret bound with $O(WT)$ total gradient evaluations. Experiments validate our theoretical findings and demonstrate the practical effectiveness of the proposed methods.
